Command: Do not eat a meal offering leavened
Summary: The command: Do not eat a meal offering leavened (Leviticus 6:17). The priests' portion of the meal offering was baked unleavened and eaten in the court of the tabernacle.
Commandment: Do not eat a meal offering leavened.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. Hebrews teaches these sacrifices could never perfect the worshiper; they pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering, which is why they ceased with the new covenant.
Purpose: To provide atonement, thanksgiving, and fellowship under the old covenant. Hebrews teaches these pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering (Hebrews 10:1-14), so the system ceased.
Function: The priests' portion of the meal offering was baked unleavened and eaten in the court — a ceremonial law about holy food kept pure. Its goal was to keep the priests' meal free of leaven, matching the altar's own rule that no leaven was burned there. It did not address a particular evil; its work was order and reverence, not restraint. The unleavened bread on the priests' table said the same thing as the unleavened bread on the altar: holy food is kept plain.
